name: Lock 11
reason: Wikivoyage Mildura plus exploremildura/Mildura council: the only Murray lock the public can walk across, island lookout over the weir; short but a named second-tier stop.

name: Apex Park
reason: Wikivoyage Mildura names it a large inland sandbar beach for swimming; Visit Mildura links it to the Chaffey Trail; a beach stop (rule: second-tier beaches keep). Objection: seasonal swimming only.

name: Meeting of the Waters
reason: Lonely Planet, Visit NSW and Wikivoyage Wentworth name the Murray-Darling junction with a viewing tower and Junction Island walk; two counted sources, a named natural landmark.

name: Australian Inland Botanic Gardens
reason: Wikivoyage Mildura plus Visit Mildura map list the free semi-arid botanic garden with cafe; half an hour or more to walk.

name: Perry Sandhills
reason: Lonely Planet and Visit NSW name the dunes near Wentworth for sandboarding and sunset photography; counted sources now found.

name: Dharnya Centre
reason: Parks Victoria and Visit Echuca Moama list the Yorta Yorta cultural centre in Barmah National Park with guided cultural experiences and walks. Objection: hours uncertain, check dharnyacentre.com.au.

name: Terrick Terrick National Park
reason: Parks Victoria and Bendigo Region tourism list the park with walks, birdwatching (Plains-wanderer), picnic and camping; a national park, own place. Objection: remote and thin facilities.

name: Swan Hill Regional Art Gallery
reason: Wikivoyage and Visit the Murray list it (naive art collection), but Visit the Murray says it is under redevelopment with a smaller display in the library; unclear if a visitable gallery now.

name: Swan Hill River Walk
reason: Wikivoyage Swan Hill: free 4.5 km riverside walk of about two hours passing the town's attractions; also Melbourne Playgrounds listing. Objection: overlaps Riverside Park and Pioneer Settlement.

name: Holden Motor Museum Echuca
reason: National Holden Motor Museum in Echuca closed in April 2024 and moved to Coffs Harbour; rule 2 (closed).

name: Shepparton Communication Tower
reason: Wikivoyage and a Visit Shepparton listing name the free observation deck (160 steps), but a Country News report says it was closed for window repairs and listed hours conflict; open status unverified.

name: KidsTown
reason: Wikivoyage Shepparton and guides describe a very large free adventure playground open nearly every day (about 150,000 visitors a year); a family draw for an hour or more.

name: Rutherglen Loops
reason: Explore Rutherglen (tourism board) and Australian Traveller list the 48 km network of walking and cycling loops linking cellar doors and Lake Moodemere; a named trail.

name: Muscat Mile De Bortoli Rutherglen Estate
reason: Explore Rutherglen and RACV name the 1886 Seppelt cellar building and Muscat Mile tasting. For: heritage building, signature regional experience. Against: a single cellar door within a wine region, not a distinct draw.

name: Pfeiffer Wines
reason: Explore Rutherglen, Visit Victoria and RACV list the cellar door, muscat blending and Muscat Mile cask tour. For: tourism-named experience. Against: an individual winery among many.

name: Yarrawonga Weir
reason: Only a weir/dam wall; tourism sources describe the lake and foreshore, not the weir as a stop. Part of Lake Mulwala (rule 3).

name: Lake Mulwala
reason: Yarrawonga Mulwala tourism board has Lake Mulwala pages: cruises (PS Cumberoona, Paradise Queen), 4.2 km foreshore walk, Chinaman's Island wetlands walk, swimming and fishing. Counted source found; the lake is the place.
